en: Did I pay far too much for the blood of the likes of you?
! It's you.
Come by the trading house again when you have time.
Did you find anything you liked?
How have you been keeping?
I think I'll go home and see my wife for a change.
Excuse me, but do we have an appointment?
No, I came unannounced.
I see. I'm sorry, but I make it a rule
not to see anyone without an appointment.
My time is precious, you see. Good day.
Is that really how it is?
I was just about to have some tea.
Do join me for a cup.
I have some rare plates from overseas.
Do have a look at them.
How did you enjoy the tea
here at the Wesseli house?
My, what a young guest we have.
And what brings you here today?
I'm looking for a present for my grandfather.
I came to find something rare from abroad.
I see. We have a great many costly,
rare goods here. I'm sure your
grandfather will find something he likes.
Please, feel free to look around
the trading house as you like.
And if you have time, perhaps some tea?
Thank you. I'll take a good look around.
do take your time looking around
until you find your grandfather's present.
When I was your age, I went to sea myself
and traveled all over the world.
are what you see on display here.
note: completes M1#3794 (slice 047), which must be a subject phrase

en: Any human would want beautiful things
nearby, surely?
note: trailing space: msg 145298 has no wait and msg 145308 (#3876) continues on the same line

en: If I must keep things close,
I'd rather they were beautiful
note: followed by 3x M1#180 '.' + M1#25 '.' = four dots; needs M1#25 variant '' for msg 145308 (slice 000)

en: That's the way I think. Why, my wife
is already my fourth.
Still,
not one woman can rival your beauty.
Rest assured.
I have no strange inclinations.
I simply love beautiful things.
An object simply sits there, beautiful,
and that alone fills my heart.
Wouldn't you say that's enough?
My wife and I had a little spat this morning.
She, too, is a willful woman. It's a trial.
Yes, I think I'll take this incense burner.
It's an import from China, isn't it?
Exactly so.
You've chosen a very fine piece.
Ah, yes,
let me add this Indian incense to it.
Please do come again.
My last voyage was to India.
There, I secured a route for importing
rare spices and textiles.
I also brought back a few rare plants
at the time, but
sadly, they withered and died.
Sorry, but I'm worn out.
Could you come back another time?
Got business with this ship?
I'm Stelan, captain of this ship.
She's a small trading ship. A bit dated,
but, well, she's lovable in her own way.
Say, have you been up to the ship's bow?
<I haven't>
note: menu option; the yes option is presumably elsewhere (not in this slice)

en: Nice view, isn't it?
You can see the whole town of Calstatt
from up there.
Well, no harm in trying. Go on up to the bow
of the ship.
What a view, I tell you!
Loading and unloading the cargo takes a while.
We won't be sailing for a bit yet.
Calstatt
note: subject only; M1#3920 (slice 049) must continue as the predicate ('was originally a small fishing village.')
